work_completed: `_scan` no longer stops on the first finding of row W2-L423's rule. It reads gitleaks' JSON report from its stdout, held in memory, with `--report-format json --report-path -` in place of `--redact`. Any finding of another rule, or any match that is not exactly 40 hex digits, still returns a finding at once, as before. When the only findings are candidate hashes, every rule set still runs (both DEC-347 configurations), and then one bounded `git cat-file --batch-check` call (10 s) is made against the project root. Git runs with every `GIT_*` variable removed, `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` set to the root's parent, `--no-replace-objects` plus `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1`, and the commit-graph off. A match is exempt only when git exits 0 and its output says that exact id is a `commit`. Tags, trees, blobs, missing objects, another repository's commits, an error exit, a timeout, no git, a root that is not a repository, or an unreadable report all stay a finding. The project root reaches `_scan` from `indexable`, `path_holds_secret` and `stores_with_secrets`; without a root nothing is exempt. The rule id is joined at run time from a tuple, and the clean-result record logic is unchanged.

risks: 1. gitleaks now runs without `--redact`, so its stdout holds matches in plain text in memory, inside the `CompletedProcess` object. If gitleaks timed out, the `TimeoutExpired` exception would carry any partial stdout as an attribute, though not in its message. gitleaks writes the report only at the end, so in practice that is empty. 2. A commit id quoted in upper case is exempt; the brief allows either outcome. 3. A file of many candidate hashes adds one git call per scanned text, up to 10 s each, inside the existing limits.
lessons: Run W2-69's acceptance folder on its own, in the background with a long timeout (it takes about 35 min), and read its output file. Builder tests that monkeypatch `_scan` must now accept a third argument (`root`).
